_comment: Authored advisory assessment register (GEN-043). One entry per advisory any scanner reports, with the decision, the REACHABILITY fact that decides it, and the observed dependency paths it was assessed against. scripts/assess-advisories.py fails when a scanner reports an advisory with no entry here, when an entry lacks a rationale/reachability/owner, when an ACCEPT entry's observed paths no longer match the scan, when a LIVE advisory is marked RESOLVED, or when an entry describes an advisory nothing reports any more (mark it RESOLVED).
reviewed: round 63: both npm advisories remediated by the vitest upgrade; register has no open advisory

assessments.title: Vitest: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via @vitest/mocker Redirect Mock
assessments.reachability: NOT SHIPPED, direct devDependency path: the scanner reports '.>vitest', i.e. vitest is a devDependency of the workspace ROOT package and is not a dependency of apps/desktop or of any crate. No test-runner code is packaged into the MSI, the NSIS setup or the executable, and the artifact lanes drive the packaged binary and the installed MSI, neither of which contains vitest.
assessments.rationale: The advisory needs a reachable Vite dev server's HMR WebSocket to register a redirect mock; the product ships no dev server, and the dev server that exists in the repository binds loopback. Fixing it requires upgrading vitest (4.1.11 or 5.x), a test-runner upgrade with its own blast radius, so it is deferred rather than ignored: the enforced audit level is --audit-level high, this finding is below it, and it is disclosed in COMMANDS.md as an accepted risk.
assessments.resolution: REMEDIATED, not waived: vitest was upgraded 3.2.7 -> 4.1.11 (the first patched version, Dependabot security PR #7) and then 4.1.11 -> 5.0.1 (PR #11), so GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9 no longer resolves in pnpm-lock.yaml. Verified: `pnpm audit` now reports 'No known vulnerabilities found' (exit 0) and GitHub marks the three corresponding Dependabot alerts (vitest x2, @vitest/mocker x1) as `fixed`. This entry is kept, with the assessment that was made at the time, because a decision about an advisory that is no longer reported must say RESOLVED rather than silently disappear.

assessments.title: Vitest: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via @vitest/mocker Redirect Mock (through @vitest/mocker)
assessments.reachability: NOT SHIPPED, transitive devDependency path: the scanner reports '.>vitest>@vitest/mocker', i.e. the vulnerable module is reached only INSIDE the vitest devDependency tree. It is the same advisory as npm:1193683 seen through the package the fix lands in, and neither the package nor the runner is packaged into any shipped artifact.
assessments.rationale: Same subject and same disposition as npm:1193683, recorded separately because the scanner reports it as its own advisory entry with its own path: the decision to defer the vitest upgrade covers both, and both paths are devDependency paths rather than shipped ones. The first version of this register marked this entry RESOLVED as a placeholder; that was false -- the scanner does report it -- and the validator did not catch it because the RESOLVED check only ran in one direction. Both are fixed.

Verified: `pnpm audit` now reports 'No known vulnerabilities found' (exit 0) and GitHub marks the three corresponding Dependabot alerts (vitest x2, @vitest/mocker x1) as `fixed`. This entry is kept, with the assessment that was made at the time, because a decision about an advisory that is no longer reported must say RESOLVED rather than silently disappear.
